newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT BREAKS RESISTANCE, CLOSES AT $18.84.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT BREAKS RESISTANCE, CLOSES AT $18.84.

text.p: IPE Brent was boosted on Tuesday by renewed strength in the U.S. gasoline market and broke through the $18.80 resistance level in a late surge to close 26 cents up at $18.84 a barrel, brokers said.
The September contract gained 10-15 cents after the NYMEX market opened but was then trapped in the $18.72-$18.79 range for much of the afternoon, bouncing off the $18.80 ceiiing and consolidating.
But a late upward spike in September gasoline, which closed 2.25 cents up at 63.72 a gallon, dragged Brent futures further into positive territory.

Some brokers were dubious as to the real vigour of Brent's late upward push, given that gasoline failed to break its 64 cent resistance target and the WTI, although closing 31 cents higher, ended perched on its target level of $20.
"We'll just have to see what the APIs bring, but we expect them to be fairly neutral," said one broker.

Weekly American Petroleum Institute data were due for release after the market closed. In recent weeks there has been heavy buying of gasoline in anticipation of bullish stock draws, in the hours before the data appears.
That pattern appeared to repeat itself on Tuesday.

Dealers in the U.S. said they expected the API report to show a fall in gasoline stocks of one to three million barrels due in part to lower output, with crude stocks expected to decline by a similar amount.
Earlier both Brent and IPE gas oil were supported by good technical factors and tight prompt physical crude markets.
They shrugged off Monday's announcement by Iraq that it wanted to export 30 million barrels of crude by end-August to help it attain its ambitious target of $1 billion worth of sales by Sept 5.
Poor initial sales of Basrah Light into the Gulf supported market scepticism about Baghdad's ability to meet its goals.
Earlier IPE September gas oil closed up $1 at $170.75 a tonne after a quiet expiry of the August contract.
"We're a dollar up but its been pretty quiet and gas oil has lost ground against practically everything else," said one broker.
